messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT DETECTED - KV cache + continuous-batching regression in us-west-2. Paging observed on a subset of serving nodes, sustained for ~3 minutes. Metrics: kv_cache_size +420%, batch_queue_depth spikes, tail latency > 1500ms for mixed requests. Pager: @aditya oncall. https://internal.incidents/2165550000

aditya: on it, waking up. seeing big jump in kv cache entries and continuous-batching backlog. paging now. starting investigation — linking dashboards.

sara: confirming - heatmap shows mixed short/long requests causing pack-shedding. lots of small requests getting starved, large requests holding KV locks. I see paging events tied to prefetch tasks.

mike: impact: some hosted customers (tier: dev & small-prod) report errors 5-12% and token latencies up to 3s on generation endpoints. No SSO failures.

jenn: can we throttle prefetch / reduce pack size? quick mitigation idea: toggle kv_cache_prefetch=false and reduce max_batch_tokens to 2048 for the serving group.

aditya: trying a quick config change on canary pool. command I ran: ```
# on infra control plane
curl -X POST https://api.redwood-internal/configs/apply \
  -d '{"pool":"usw2-inference-canary","kv_cache_prefetch":false,"batch.max_tokens":2048}' 
```

incident-bot: deploy-bot: config apply started for usw2-canary (job id: cfg-2165550000-1).

sara: watch queues — if continuous-batching backlog drops within 30s we can roll to primary. also lowering scheduler.mix_threshold to 0.25 might help fairness between long/short.

aditya: canary looks promising: backlog down 40%, tail latency trending down to ~600ms. paging events reduced. rolling to 30% of pool now.

mike: customer-facing note: scaling team notified. estimate containment in 15-20m if roll holds. would recommend sending a brief status update to affected customers (PSAT ticket group).

jenn: issuing small rollback on prefetch globally is low-risk; preparing rollout play: 1) apply prefetch=false to primary 2) reduce batch max 3) adjust scheduler thresholds 4) monitor for 10m 5) revert if errors increase.

aditya: rolling to primary now. commands: ```
kubectl apply -f /ops/configs/usw2-batching-hotfix.yaml
# contents: kv_cache_prefetch: false\n# batch.max_tokens: 2048\n# scheduler.mix_threshold: 0.25
```

ops-sre: monitor note: watch these metrics: `kv_cache_entries`, `continuous_batch_backlog`, `scheduler_queue_depth_short`, `scheduler_queue_depth_long`, `paging_events/sec`, `gen_error_rate`. Alert if paging_events/sec > 1 for > 60s.

incident-bot: NOTE - rollback-safety window 10m. If gen_error_rate rises >3% revert prefetch immediately.

aditya: primary rollout complete at +8m. initial telemetry: kv_cache entries stabilized, backlog -55%, paging_events down to baseline. still seeing tail latency ~450ms but trending.

sara: quick root-cause notes: a combination of a recent batching tweak (pack-size heuristics) + prefetch enabled caused KV hot-shards to hold locks on long requests; mixed traffic amplified pack starvation. need follow-up: decouple prefetch from pack ownership and add KV lock timeouts.

mike: customer impact summary for ops: ~6% of gen requests for small subset of customers experienced latency or 5xx between 21:10-21:30 UTC (approx). No data exfiltration.

oncall-t2: taking handoff for next 2 hours. summary: mitigation applied (prefetch off, max_tokens=2048, scheduler.mix_threshold=0.25), metrics are stable. next steps: postmortem, config rollback plan after code fix, add automated runbook step to auto-throttle prefetch when kv_cache_entries slope > 2000/min.

aditya: adding TODOs to incident doc and tagging eng-runtime + eng-ml. I'll coordinate postmortem. thanks all. :thumbsup:
